items.title: The pinned GFM corpus matches 582 of 672 exact HTML examples (86.6%); 90 deviations are documented
items.expected: Verify each behavior against cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13 / markdown-it 15.0.3; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: The pinned GFM corpus matches **582 of 672 exact HTML examples (86.6%)**; **90 deviations** are documented. These include serialization differences in void tags, task-list classes, and highlighted code, as well as differences in reference resolution, tables, nested emphasis, raw HTML, escapes, and extended autolinks. The guide lists the affected specification sections and counts.

The guide lists the affected specification sections and counts.

items.title: Explicit assignments take priority
items.expected: Verify each behavior against public Calca reference; licensed-app verification still needed; separate deliberate policy from unsupported upstream capabilities.
items.disclosure: Explicit assignments take priority. Queries look backward for the most recent usable equation and may skip unsupported or underdetermined relations. This is not a simultaneous-equation consistency checker. Derived answers are not stored as assignments. An expression depending on multiple or no roots reports a diagnostic rather than choosing a root; query the unknown directly instead. Identities report infinitely many solutions rather than selecting an answer.

Identities report infinitely many solutions rather than selecting an answer.

items.baselineDisclosure: Numeric definitions use assignment-time values; unresolved definitions use current values when queried. Reassignment is allowed, headings do not create scopes, and state resets on every render. These behaviors differ from Calca.

items.title: Calculation and literal Markdown block isolation
items.expected: The explicit Sheets structured-block profile isolates literal Markdown input, executes supported calculation blocks, and retains original source locations. Unprofiled documents keep legacy behavior.
items.disclosure: Structured blocks (calca-blocks-v1) uses parsed Markdown boundaries: only calca-labelled fences, indented code, and standalone paragraph arrow expressions calculate. Literal language/unlabelled fences, TeX, Mermaid, inline code/math, headings, links, and HTML do not run as calculations. Legacy remains the default for unprofiled URLs and version-1 saved documents. This resolves Markdown block isolation in the explicit profile; it does not implement Calca’s complete input grammar.
items.baselineDisclosure: Every fenced or indented code block is calculation input, regardless of its language label. Literal code, math, or Mermaid fences can therefore produce calculation diagnostics. Arrow answers replace text in the preview; the editor source is retained. Built-in unit/constant names can conflict with unknown names.

items.title: Decimal arithmetic and precision tolerances
items.expected: Exact decimal quantities and supported tolerance rules agree with the pinned independent reference.
items.disclosure: Amounts are preserved as decimal values with a 28-significant-digit, half-even arithmetic context. Transactions infer commodity tolerances; supported options control the multiplier, defaults, and cost/price contributions. Balance assertions support inferred and explicit tolerances. Earlier versions used a fixed 1e-8 transaction tolerance and binary numbers; reports also rounded to eight decimal places. These precision gaps are resolved for the supported syntax.
items.baselineDisclosure: Arithmetic uses JavaScript numbers and a fixed **1e-8 transaction tolerance**, rather than Beancount's exact Decimal arithmetic and inferred tolerances. Upstream tolerance and rounding rules are not fully implemented.

items.title: Reserved names and remaining input grammar
items.expected: Audit remaining input grammar against Calca’s public reference and a licensed app; preserve deliberate expression guards.
items.disclosure: Both profiles still evaluate one line at a time. Indentation-based multiline definitions, named arguments, multiple statements per line, and the original app’s broader prose/calculation inference remain unsupported. Built-in unit/constant names can conflict with unknown names; use distinct identifiers. Arrow answers replace preview text while the editor source remains intact.
items.baselineDisclosure: Every fenced or indented code block is calculation input, regardless of its language label. Literal code, math, or Mermaid fences can therefore produce calculation diagnostics. Arrow answers replace text in the preview; the editor source is retained. Built-in unit/constant names can conflict with unknown names.
